[IRET.10.5] **Withdraw action.** `withdraw b` lowers to an `ACTION_WITHDRAW`
whose `withdraw_pattern_index` is `b`'s position in the activation token
([RDSC.4a.8]). At fire time the engine **must** retract the fact at that
position as an engine retraction: the fact leaves working memory, the retraction
propagates through the network as any other does ([IRET.7.8]), and the stream
records it as a `FactWithdraw` with cause `AUTHOR_WITHDRAWN` ([RFCS.7a.2]). If
the fact is no longer live when the action runs, the action does nothing.

The action does not end the firing. The actions after it run, and none of them
refers to the withdrawn fact, because the compiler refuses one that would
([LGRA.10.1.3]).
